Model & numerical assumptions

Planar diffusion: ∂c/∂t = ∇·(D∇c). A conservative finite-volume grid uses harmonic face diffusivities and an explicit stability-limited timestep. Concentration and flux are continuous across media interfaces (partition coefficient 1). Solid faces have zero flux. Sensors are passive.

The upper exterior extends to x = ±4 mm and y = 4 mm, with c = 0 on its distant edges: a finite approximation of an initially empty infinite medium. The curved interface is permeable and has no added layer. The lower rectangular fluid chamber spans the diameter and extends 0.8 mm beyond the wall; its outer edges are sealed. The flat edge outside the chamber is sealed.

Grid spacing: 0.025 mm. Geometry is snapped to cells; sources and sensors occupy a single cell. Concentration is in arbitrary units; source amount is the area integral of concentration per unit out-of-plane depth. Holes are centered symmetrically; center spacing must exceed hole width. The plotted profile samples y = 0.0125 mm; sensors sample the first fluid row beyond the wall. These are approximate point sources and point sensors. For quantitative work, check grid and exterior-domain convergence.
